answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each claimed identity to complete a challenge-specific chain of sequential modular squarings before its proof is accepted. The inlet, sable, and prism labels can domain-separate challenges; they do not remove the dependency between squarings. GPUs can run separate chains concurrently, but cannot shortcut one chain, so creating clones multiplies the required work and preserves a wall-clock bottleneck. Wesolowski proofs let verifiers check each result efficiently.
